description: The optional Features an application may apply to its objects (metamodel/feature.md). Generated by scripts/compile-optional-features.mjs; edit the Feature files.

features.name: Aggregate Transaction
features.description: An operation happens completely or not at all: if any check fails, nothing is changed.
features.meaning: One transaction locks the aggregate and its collaborating rows in a stable order, re-reads what it depends on, checks authorization, lifecycle and rules, writes, and appends history before commit.

promises.text: When any check fails, nothing of the operation is stored.
Checks see the rows as they are written, not a stale read.

features.name: Asynchronous Operation
features.description: A long operation is accepted at once and finishes in the background, and people can see how it went.
features.meaning: The request is accepted with a tracking id; the work runs after; its status (pending, done, failed) and result can be read.

promises.text: The operation is accepted at once with a tracking id.
Its status and result can be read until it completes.
A failure is reported, never lost.

features.name: Pagination
features.description: Lists come a page at a time, can be filtered and sorted, and always in the same order; people see, and count, only the records they are allowed to.
features.meaning: A collection read takes allowed filters, a sort and a page; the sort is stable (the id breaks ties); it returns the items, the total, the page and its size; access scope applies before counting, filtering or paging.

promises.text: The same read returns the same order, page after page.
The total counts only the records the user may see.
Only the allowed attributes can be filtered on; others are refused.

features.name: Partial Update
features.description: A form changes only the fields people may edit: the system sets ids, statuses and timestamps itself, and a change leaves every other field as it was.
features.meaning: Create takes the business attributes only; the service sets the id, the initial status and system values. Update is a patch of editable attributes: omitted fields keep their values; system fields in a request are refused.

promises.text: Fields left out of an update keep their values.
A request setting a system field (id, status, timestamps) is refused.

features.name: Search
features.description: People find records by typing what they remember of them.
features.meaning: A text query matches the record's searchable attributes and its label; results respect access scope and soft delete.

promises.text: A record is found by text from its searchable attributes or label.
Results include only records the user may see.

features.name: Standard Errors
features.description: Every refusal says why with a fixed code (invalid input, not allowed, not found, changed by someone else, duplicate, or a business rule) and never shows internals.
features.meaning: Refusals map to fixed codes: invalid input 400, unauthenticated 401, forbidden 403, not found 404, stale version 409 conflict, duplicate 409, business rule 422 naming the rule; no stack trace or SQL reaches the client.

promises.text: Each kind of refusal has its fixed status and code.
A business-rule refusal names the rule.
No refusal shows internals (stack, SQL).

features.name: State Machine
features.description: A record moves through named statuses by its operations; an action applies only from the right status, and doing it twice is refused.
features.meaning: Each transition names its source and target statuses. A transition compares the stored status with its source; a repeated or late command whose source no longer matches is refused, with no duplicate history or event.

promises.text: An operation succeeds from its source status and leaves the target status.
From any other status it is refused, and nothing changes.
Repeating a transition is refused, with no duplicate history or event.

features.name: Annotations
features.description: People leave notes on the pages of the application, on a document or a page element.
features.meaning: An annotation is attached to a page or an element of it, has an author and a state, and is the author's own unless shared.

parameters.name: sharing
parameters.description: Users may share a note with everyone who can see its page or record; false keeps every note private to its author.

promises.text: An annotation stays attached to the element it was left on.
An annotation is visible to its author, and to others only when shared.
An annotation can be marked done.

features.name: Assignment
features.description: A record is assigned to a person who is responsible for it.
features.meaning: A record has an assignee, set and changed by those allowed to; the assignee sees it among their work.

promises.text: Assigning a record makes that person its assignee.
The assignee sees the record among their work.
Only those allowed can assign or reassign.

features.name: Bookmarks
features.description: People keep their own list of records to come back to.
features.meaning: A user marks a record of a bookmarkable entity and reaches it again from anywhere; the list is the user's own; a record the user can no longer see shows as unavailable.

promises.text: A user sees only their own bookmarks, by the record's label.
A bookmark is added and removed from the record's page.
A bookmarked record the user can no longer see is shown as unavailable, without its label.

features.name: Comments
features.description: People discuss a record in comments kept with it.
features.meaning: A comment has an author, a time and text, belongs to one record, and is shown with it to those who may see the record.

promises.text: A comment is shown with its record, with its author and time.
Only those who may see the record see its comments.

features.name: Following
features.description: People follow a record to hear about its changes.
features.meaning: A user follows or unfollows a record; followers are notified of its changes.

promises.text: A user can follow and unfollow a record.
Followers are notified when the record changes.

features.name: Inbox
features.description: Each person has one place listing what needs their attention.
features.meaning: Items addressed to a user (assignments, mentions, notifications) gather in their inbox, newest first, marked read or unread.

promises.text: A user sees only the items addressed to them.
Opening an item marks it read.
Items are listed newest first.

features.name: Mentions
features.description: Naming a person in a comment or message tells them.
features.meaning: An @-mention of a user in text the record holds notifies that user, if they may see the record.

promises.text: A mentioned user is notified.
A user who may not see the record is not notified and gains no access.

features.name: Messaging
features.description: People send messages to each other, or about a record.
features.meaning: A message has a sender, recipients and a body, optionally about a record; recipients see it in their inbox.

promises.text: Each recipient sees a sent message.
A message about a record is shown with that record to those who may see it.

features.name: Notifications
features.description: People are told when something they care about happens.
features.meaning: A committed business event notifies the people the requirements name, through the channels configured; a failed notification never undoes the change.

promises.text: The people the requirements name are notified of the event.
No notification is sent for a change that rolled back.
A failed notification does not undo the change.

features.name: Outbox
features.description: What the application sends out is recorded with the change that caused it and delivered reliably, after that change is saved.
features.meaning: A message or business event to send is written in the same transaction as the change; it is delivered after commit, retried on failure, and never sent for a change that rolled back.

promises.text: Nothing is sent for a change that rolled back.
A committed change's messages are delivered.
A failed delivery is retried and never undoes the change.

features.name: Save for Later
features.description: People can stop part-way and come back to finish, without losing what they entered.
features.meaning: An unfinished record or use case is kept as the user's draft, invisible to others and outside the business rules until it is completed.

promises.text: A saved draft is kept and resumed with what was entered.
Others do not see a user's draft.
Business rules apply when the draft is completed, not before.

features.name: Sharing
features.description: A person can share a record with others, who then see it.
features.meaning: Sharing grants named people access to one record, within what their roles allow; it can be withdrawn.

promises.text: A person a record is shared with can see it.
Sharing never grants more than the recipient's role allows.
Withdrawing a share removes the access.

features.name: Tags
features.description: People label records freely to find them again.
features.meaning: A record carries tags from a free or controlled vocabulary, personal or shared as chosen; records can be listed by tag.

parameters.name: vocabulary
parameters.description: free = users type new tags as they go; controlled = tags are chosen from a list a role maintains.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: shared = everyone sees an instance's tags; personal = each user's tags are their own.

promises.text: A tagged record is found by its tag.
With a controlled vocabulary, a tag outside it is refused.
Personal tags are seen only by their owner.

features.name: Attachments
features.description: Files are attached to a record and downloaded again.
features.meaning: An attachment attribute holds files with their name, type and size; they are stored outside the row and served only to those who may see the record.

promises.text: An attached file is downloaded unchanged.
Only those who may see the record can download its files.

features.name: Audit Trail
features.description: Each record says when it was created and changed, and, as chosen, by whom, and keeps its history.
features.meaning: Creation and update times (and, as chosen, the users) are set by the system from the request's context, never taken from the client; the history option keeps state or full history.

parameters.name: created
parameters.description: Record when an instance was created.

parameters.name: updated
parameters.description: Record when an instance was last updated.

parameters.name: updatedBy
parameters.description: Record who last updated an instance.

parameters.name: history
parameters.description: none = timestamps only; state = state value/date history; full = complete entity history.

promises.text: Creation and update times (and users, when chosen) are set by the system, not the client.
A change updates the update time (and user).
With history, each change is recorded and readable.

features.name: Business Journal
features.description: Business events, such as a request submitted or a sale activated, are written to the business journal as they happen.
features.meaning: An occurrence is appended to the journal for each business event the entity's transitions raise, as the architecture's journal requires.

promises.text: Each business event of the entity is appended to the journal.
No occurrence remains for a change that rolled back.

features.name: Foreign-key Indexes
features.description: Every link between records can be followed quickly: each foreign key has an index.
features.meaning: Every foreign-key column has an index; a composite index with that column first counts.

promises.text: Every foreign-key column has an index in the migrated database.

features.name: Hierarchy
features.description: Records nest under a parent of the same kind, to any depth, always within the same parent record and never in a loop.
features.meaning: A record may have a parent of the same entity within the same scope. Reparenting checks the ancestors and refuses a cycle; the depth limit and leaf rules are parameters.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: The relationship to the parent instance.

parameters.name: maxDepth
parameters.description: The deepest level allowed; 0 = no limit.

parameters.name: leafOnly
parameters.description: Only instances with no children may be used elsewhere (for example only a leaf category may be given to a product).

parameters.name: deleteWithChildren
parameters.description: What deleting an instance with children does: refuse it, delete the branch, or give the children the deleted instance's parent.

promises.text: Making a record its own ancestor is refused.
A parent outside the record's scope is refused.
When a depth limit is set, nesting beyond it is refused.

features.name: Immutable Record
features.description: Once written, these records are never changed or deleted.
features.meaning: Records are only inserted and read: no update or delete exists, through the API or the writer.

promises.text: Changing a written record is refused.
Deleting a written record is refused.

features.name: Last Write Wins
features.description: For simple records, the latest saved edit wins; rules that span records are still protected by locking.
features.meaning: No version token: scalar edits keep the last accepted write, and the aggregate's row locks protect the rules that span records.

promises.text: Of two edits, the later one is kept.
A rule spanning records still holds under concurrent edits.

features.name: Optimistic Concurrency
features.description: Two people editing the same record cannot silently overwrite each other: the second save is refused and asked to refresh.
features.meaning: Every write of the record carries the version it read. The write compares it with the stored version and increments it; a stale version is refused as a conflict, and nothing is written.

parameters.name: versionField
parameters.description: The attribute that holds the version token.

promises.text: A successful write increments the version.
A write with a stale version is refused with a conflict, and nothing of it is stored.
Two concurrent writes from the same version never both succeed.

features.name: Ordering
features.description: Items keep a numbered order (1, 2, 3…): new ones go last, and people can rearrange the whole list at once.
features.meaning: Siblings carry a sequence within their parent. A new sibling goes last; a reorder gives the complete ordered list of siblings and rewrites the sequence in one change; a stale or incomplete list is refused.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The child attribute that holds the item's position (for example lineNo).

parameters.name: reorder
parameters.description: Users may move items to a new position; false fixes the order of entry.

parameters.name: numbering
parameters.description: sequential = positions 1, 2, 3 renumbered after every change; gapped = 10, 20, 30, so an inserted item takes a free number and the others keep theirs (line numbers others quote).

promises.text: A new item is placed last.
A reorder with the complete list renumbers every item in that order.
A reorder that leaves out an item, or comes from a stale list, is refused and changes nothing.

features.name: Polymorphic Reference
features.description: One link that can point at different kinds of record, always at one that exists.
features.meaning: A reference names its target's kind in a type column; the service verifies, in the same transaction, that the target exists in the table the type selects.

promises.text: A reference to a record that does not exist is refused.
A reference to a kind it does not allow is refused.

features.name: Restricted Delete
features.description: A record that others still refer to cannot be deleted, and nothing is purged behind anyone's back.
features.meaning: Deletion keeps every reference: foreign keys restrict, the business rules are checked before deleting, and nothing is purged or expires.

promises.text: Deleting a record others refer to is refused, and nothing changes.
A record nothing refers to is deleted when its business rules allow.

features.name: Single Primary
features.description: Exactly one child is the primary one, such as a customer's main contact; naming a new one replaces the old.
features.meaning: Exactly one child per parent is flagged primary at every commit; naming a new primary clears the old one in the same change.

promises.text: A parent with children always has exactly one primary.
Naming a new primary clears the old one.

features.name: Soft Delete
features.description: Deleting keeps the record, marked with when it was deactivated: it leaves the lists, and its history and links stay readable.
features.meaning: Delete marks the record deactivated, with the time; lists and searches leave it out by default; reads by id and the records that refer to it still see it.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The attribute that records when the record was deactivated.

promises.text: A deleted record still exists, with when it was deactivated.
A deleted record no longer appears in lists or searches.
Records that refer to a deleted record still show it.

features.name: Status History
features.description: Every status change is recorded (from what, to what, by whom, when and why), starting with the record's first status.
features.meaning: The history gets an entry for the initial status and every transition, with the actor and time from the request's context and the operation's reason.

promises.text: Creating a record records its first status.
Each transition records from, to, who, when and why.
A refused or rolled-back transition leaves no entry.

features.name: Storage Naming
features.description: Tables and columns are named from the model by one convention, so storage names are never written down twice.
features.meaning: A table is the entity's name in the convention's case plus a plural suffix, and a column its attribute's name; a capability design gives a storage name only where it differs.

promises.text: Every table and column is named by the convention, or by the design where it differs.

features.name: Own Records Only
features.description: A person sees and works on only their own records, such as a technician's profile and the requests assigned to them.
features.meaning: For the roles it applies to, reads and writes are limited to the records the principal owns or is assigned to.

promises.text: The user sees their own records.
Others' records are neither listed nor readable by id.
Changing another's record is refused.

features.name: Role-based Access
features.description: What someone may do follows from their role, as the use cases give it; every operation checks it.
features.meaning: Authority comes from the signed-in principal's roles, checked for every operation against the Authorization derived from the use cases; anything the browser sends about roles is never trusted.

promises.text: A role the use cases permit can perform the operation.
A role they do not permit is refused, and nothing changes.
A role claimed by the client is never trusted.
